scams.name: Jakarta Soekarno-Hatta Airport (CGK) Taxi Overcharge & Airport Sharks
scams.description: Soekarno-Hatta Airport (CGK) has one of Southeast Asia's most-documented 2025 tourist-taxi overcharge problems. Community reports document the pattern: drivers approach at arrivals offering 'premium' or 'VIP' rides quoting fixed prices 4–8x the legitimate Blue Bird or Grab rate. The 2025 community baseline confirms Grab and Gojek are the ONLY reliable price-transparent options for foreigners at CGK. The specific Terminal 3 pattern: 'sharks' wearing hotel-uniform-style polos wait past the customs exit, approach Western tourists and say 'Taxi, sir? Grab not allowed here, I take you.' They walk the tourist to a parking-level unmarked sedan and then charge 500K–1.5M IDR (US$30–$95) to Kuningan, Menteng, or South Jakarta — the legitimate Blue Bird meter or Grab rate is 150K–250K IDR (US$10–$16). A separate variant operates at the 'Premium Taxi' kiosks that are real but heavily overpriced (450K–700K flat) and marketed as 'safer'. Community reports document that even regular-looking taxi queues sometimes stage 'broken meter' routines then demand cash-only large bills. For older travellers, the defensive protocol: (1) ignore EVERY approach inside the terminal and in the covered walkway — all official pickup happens outdoors at the clearly-signposted Blue Bird Group counter or the Grab/Gojek pickup zones (look for 'Grab Lounge' signs); (2) book Grab or Gojek yourself on airport Wi-Fi AFTER collecting luggage and verify licence plate; (3) if using metered taxi, insist ONLY on Blue Bird (bright blue, 'Blue Bird' logo, not just any blue car) or Silver Bird (black, premium-metered); (4) legitimate fare CGK to central Jakarta is 150K–250K IDR via Grab, 200K–300K via metered Blue Bird; NEVER accept 'fixed price' quotes; (5) request a receipt (bukti); real drivers will issue one instantly via the app or a printed slip.
scams.avoidance: Use Grab or Gojek app booked on airport Wi-Fi AFTER luggage; verify licence plate For metered taxi, insist ONLY on Blue Bird (bright blue) or Silver Bird (black) — outdoor queue Typical fare CGK to central Jakarta: 150K–250K IDR Grab, 200K–300K Blue Bird IGNORE every 'taxi sir' approach inside terminal — all official pickup is outdoors Refuse 'Premium Taxi' kiosks and cash-only fixed-price quotes
scams.location: Soekarno-Hatta International Airport (CGK) arrivals Terminals 1/2/3, 'Premium Taxi' kiosk zones, Kuningan and Menteng drop-off points

scams.name: Jakarta Blue Bird Taxi Impersonator & Meter Tampering
scams.description: Jakarta has a long-running 2025 Blue Bird IMPERSONATOR problem — blue-painted non-Blue-Bird taxis with near-identical logos and 'Blue Bird' or 'Blue Bird Taxi' stickers that are not affiliated with the legitimate Blue Bird Group. Community reports document how tourists routinely mistake any blue-painted car for the real thing. The real Blue Bird Group is one of Asia's largest and safest taxi operators — registered vehicles have a specific baby-blue shade, a logo with a flying bluebird silhouette, a vehicle number painted in white on the doors, and a driver ID card prominently displayed on the dashboard. Impersonators use slightly-different fonts, generic 'TAXI' labels, and have tampered meters that tick 1.5x–2x faster than the legal 4,000 IDR flag-drop + 3,750 IDR/km rate. Community reports document related sleight-of-hand: drivers cancel the Grab ride mid-trip and demand 2–3x cash. Community reports also document the hotel-taxi rank pattern where bellhops direct tourists to a specific 'convenient' taxi (kickback paid by impersonator). Rides that should cost 30K–80K IDR end up 150K–300K; longer trips across the TransJakarta corridor can reach 500K+. For older travellers, the practical defence: (1) use the Blue Bird app or Grab/Gojek to book in-app; never flag a random blue taxi from the street or hotel rank; (2) verify the specific bluebird-silhouette logo and the 'BLUE BIRD GROUP' text, AND the driver ID card on dashboard; (3) confirm flag-drop starts at 7,500 IDR (Silver Bird) or 6,500 IDR (Blue Bird standard); (4) refuse any driver who refuses to start the meter or claims 'meter rosak' (broken meter); (5) if in doubt, walk 100m away from any hotel entrance and book Grab instead — hotel-rank kickback markups are universal; (6) save the Blue Bird customer line (+62 21 7917 1234) and request complaint/compensation for proven meter tampering.
scams.avoidance: Book via Blue Bird app OR Grab/Gojek — never flag from street or hotel rank Verify bluebird-silhouette logo + 'BLUE BIRD GROUP' text + driver ID card Confirm flag-drop starts at 6,500–7,500 IDR before moving Refuse 'meter broken' claims; get out and walk 100m to book Grab Save Blue Bird customer line (+62 21 7917 1234) for mid-trip complaints
scams.location: Hotel taxi ranks outside Grand Hyatt/Mandarin Oriental/Shangri-La Jakarta, Plaza Indonesia, Thamrin/Sudirman corridor, mall exits (Plaza Senayan, Grand Indonesia)

scams.name: Jakarta Grab/Gojek Off-App Cash-Negotiation Scam
scams.description: A 2025-surging Jakarta variant is the 'Grab off-app' scam where drivers accept your booking, confirm the pickup, then cancel the app ride on arrival and demand 2–3x the app fare in cash. Travelers describe the pattern: the driver claims 'traffic bad, I need 150K instead of 45K' or 'long distance, app price wrong, 200K cash' AFTER you've already loaded luggage. 2025 community reports confirm that both Indonesian and foreign passengers increasingly refuse to ride once cancellation is requested. The variant targeting foreigners specifically: the driver accepts the Grab booking, messages 'please wait 5 min' in-app, then arrives saying 'WhatsApp only, app broken' and quotes cash. If you complain via app they'll sometimes say 'I mark complete when you pay'. Another 2025 version is the 'Gojek motorbike' cash upsell where drivers claim petrol prices went up and demand 20K–50K extra. Community reports note scammers target solo Western tourists at airport covered walkways AFTER you book a Grab, intercepting with 'Grab cancelled, I take you same price' then charging 4x. For older travellers, the practical defence: (1) if the driver requests cancellation or says 'app broken', simply refuse and cancel yourself — Grab does not charge cancellation for driver-initiated issues; book again; (2) never hand over luggage before the driver starts the in-app trip and you confirm the app shows 'ride in progress'; (3) pay in-app via GrabPay linked to your credit card (Indonesian Rupiah auto-conversion), not cash — this prevents any mid-trip negotiation; (4) if driver insists on cash, photograph the licence plate and driver photo and report via in-app 'Emergency' button; Grab refunds 100% for proven off-app attempts; (5) for Gojek motorbike, same rules — GoPay wallet only, no cash.
scams.avoidance: Pay in-app via GrabPay/GoPay linked to your credit card — never cash Cancel any driver who says 'app broken' or requests off-app — book again Don't load luggage until app shows 'ride in progress' Use Grab's in-app 'Emergency' button to report off-app pressure Refuse all mid-trip fare adjustments; Grab refunds proven scams 100%
scams.location: Pick-up zones at malls (Grand Indonesia, Plaza Indonesia, Plaza Senayan), tourist landmarks (Monas, Kota Tua), hotel lobbies, airport covered walkways

scams.name: Jakarta ATM Skimming & Card-Cloning Fraud
scams.description: Jakarta shares Bali's ATM-skimming problem but concentrated in mall and convenience-store freestanding machines. Community reports document the baseline: 'ATM skimmers are common, especially at malls and convenience stores. Use only bank-branch ATMs.' The pattern: a physical card-reader overlay is installed over the legitimate slot at a freestanding ATM (typically overnight), a pinhole camera captures PIN entry from above or via a fake brochure holder, and within 30–90 minutes of skimming, cloned cards are used for international withdrawals. The 2025 Jakarta-specific hotspots are the Grand Indonesia / Plaza Indonesia ATM corridors (where rotating criminal crews target weekend-tourist traffic) and petrol-station ATMs in South Jakarta. Community reports document that even branch ATMs during off-hours (after 6 PM) sometimes see overnight skimmer installations. Amounts stolen range from Rp 2M (US$125) for daily-limit card withdrawals to US$2,000+ for cards with weak fraud detection. Thieves also run RFID-skimming variants targeting contactless cards in restaurants. For older travellers, the practical defence: (1) use ONLY ATMs INSIDE bank branches (BCA, Mandiri, BNI, BRI, CIMB Niaga) during business hours (8 AM–4 PM Mon–Fri) — never mall or convenience-store ATMs; (2) cover the keypad with your other hand when entering PIN; (3) wiggle the card slot before inserting — real slots don't move; legitimate readers have no loose overlays; (4) use RFID-blocking wallet or sleeve for contactless cards; (5) set low daily withdrawal limits and transaction alerts on your bank app; (6) keep one dedicated travel debit card separate from your main account; (7) if skimmed, file a formal complaint with Polda Metro Jaya (+62 21 523 4000) within 24 hours and contact your bank's emergency line for chargeback documentation.
scams.avoidance: Use ONLY bank-branch ATMs during business hours (BCA, Mandiri, BNI, BRI, CIMB) Cover keypad with other hand when entering PIN Wiggle the card slot before inserting — real ones don't move Use RFID-blocking wallet for contactless cards Set low daily withdrawal limits and transaction alerts on bank app
scams.location: Standalone ATMs at malls (Grand Indonesia, Plaza Indonesia), convenience stores (Indomaret, Alfamart), hotel lobbies without CCTV, petrol-station ATM booths

scams.name: Jakarta Kota Tua Tout-Led Becak & Bajaj Tourist Tour Scam
scams.description: Kota Tua (Old Batavia) is Jakarta's #1 day-tripper destination and hosts an entrenched becak (three-wheeled cycle rickshaw) and bajaj (auto-rickshaw) tout network. Community reports document the pattern and 2025 community frustration. The standard opener: a friendly-looking older man approaches with 'Where from? USA? I give good tour, 50K rupiah, Kota Tua all places.' The agreed 50K balloons to 250K–500K (US$15–$30) by the end via 'additional stops' (wayang museum 30K, harbour 50K, selfie at cannon 25K, 'tip for me' 100K). Community reports document the broader Indonesian tout pattern. The Kota Tua variant specifically targets Western cruise-ship day-trippers from Tanjung Priok via pre-positioned touts at the Fatahillah entrance. Secondary scam: 'photo-with-cannon' and 'Dutch uniform rental' where costumed locals pose tourists for photos at 25K–50K per person (stated) but demand 200K+ for a 'group family shot' AFTER photos are taken. Community reports document the 2025 government-crackdown parallel for this pattern across Java tourist zones. For older travellers, the practical defence: (1) walk Kota Tua on foot — the whole square is 500m × 400m and Fatahillah Square, Wayang Museum, Jakarta History Museum, Café Batavia, and Bank Mandiri Museum are all within 5-minute walks; (2) refuse EVERY becak/bajaj tour offer — there is no 'tour route' worth taking; individual museums cost only Rp 5K–25K entry; (3) for transfers to/from Kota Tua, use Grab to the exact entrance (Jalan Taman Fatahillah); (4) photograph with the cannon yourself — do NOT accept unsolicited offers from costumed locals; (5) for the Sunda Kelapa harbour (phinisi schooner boats), book through a licensed operator via Klook or your hotel concierge (not a tout at the entrance); (6) Kota Tua's best cheap eat is the warung near Bank Mandiri Museum — not Café Batavia (overpriced tourist-trap menu).
scams.avoidance: Walk Kota Tua on foot — everything worth seeing is within 5 min Refuse ALL becak/bajaj tour offers; individual museum entries are 5K–25K IDR Use Grab for transfer to Jalan Taman Fatahillah entrance NEVER accept photo offers from costumed 'Dutch soldiers' or Vespa owners Book Sunda Kelapa harbour visits via Klook/hotel, not tour touts
scams.location: Fatahillah Square (Kota Tua old town), around Café Batavia, Sunda Kelapa harbour approach, Wayang Museum exit

scams.name: Jakarta Honeypot Bar / KTV Overcharge & Tinder Extortion (Blok M / Kemang)
scams.description: Jakarta's Blok M and Kemang nightlife districts host a documented 2025 'honeypot bar' pattern where solo male Western tourists are targeted via Tinder, Bumble, or Badoo matches who insist on meeting at a specific venue. Community reports describe the extortion pattern. The date picks an unmarked upstairs bar or KTV (karaoke-bar) room; 2–3 'hostesses' join the table uninvited; bottles of mid-shelf whisky priced at Rp 4M–15M (US$250–$950) appear automatically. At check-out the bill runs Rp 15M–40M (US$950–$2,500) and bouncers block the exit until credit-card payment is processed. The related Blok M scam variant targets regular bar-hoppers: 'girl-friendly' bars charge a posted Rp 80K beer price but when the guest invites a hostess to sit, every subsequent drink for her (and secretly for the bar staff) is charged at Rp 500K–1M. Community reports warn specifically about Jakarta nightlife traps. A 2025 variant uses immigration-threats: community reports document how some bars threaten to call immigration on the tourist (claiming the hostess is underage) to extract higher 'settlement' fees. For older solo male travellers, the practical defence: (1) NEVER let a dating-app match pick the venue — YOU choose a reputable public bar with published menu prices and visible security cameras (Kilo Lounge, Awan Lounge in Senopati, Cork & Screw in Kemang); (2) ALWAYS ask for the written menu BEFORE ordering, and photograph each page; (3) refuse any 'hostess' joining your table uninvited — ask them to leave or depart yourself; (4) if a bill arrives with surprise charges, pay with a credit card ONLY, then dispute via your issuer the next day (chargeback will succeed with photographed menu); (5) save the Indonesian Tourist Police (Polisi Pariwisata) number: +62 21 570 9111 and Jakarta embassy emergency contacts; (6) community reports note that immigration will NOT arrest foreign tourists over bar-hostess disputes — threats are extortion bluff.
scams.avoidance: YOU pick the venue — reputable named bars: Kilo Lounge, Awan, Cork & Screw Ask for written menu BEFORE ordering; photograph every page Refuse hostesses who join your table uninvited Pay with credit card only, then dispute via chargeback with photo evidence Save Polisi Pariwisata (+62 21 570 9111); immigration threats are extortion bluff
scams.location: Blok M bar district, Kemang nightlife strip, Jalan Falatehan, Melawai/Senopati bars, 'girl-friendly' Tinder date venues in Kemang/SCBD
